claims.claim: ⚠️ **Orbital cellulitis is an emergency** with complications including intracranial infection, cavernous sinus thrombosis and vision loss.
claims.source_text: Orbital cellulitis is an emergency with serious complications including intracranial infection, cavernous sinus thrombosis and vision loss
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Orbital = postseptal** (behind the orbital septum), and over 80% relate to local sinus disease. **Periorbital = preseptal** — eyelids and surrounding skin, not the orbit. **The globe is not involved in either.**
claims.source_text: infection within the orbit, (ie postseptal, the structures posterior to the orbital septum) … the majority (>80%) of cases relate to local sinus disease … infection of the eye lids and surrounding skin not involving the orbit (ie preseptal, the structures anterior to the orbital septum) … The globe is not involved in either infection
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The two overlap clinically and can be hard to tell apart.** Typical presentation: unilateral eyelid swelling and erythema, with unilateral eye pain or tenderness.
claims.source_text: Periorbital and orbital cellulitis are distinct clinical diseases, though have overlapping clinical features and therefore can be difficult to differentiate … Unilateral eyelid swelling and erythema Unilateral eye pain or tenderness
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Red flags for orbital cellulitis:** painful or restricted eye movements · reduced acuity, relative afferent pupil defect or diplopia · proptosis · severe headache or other signs of intracranial involvement.
claims.source_text: Red flags concerning for orbital cellulitis Painful or restricted eye movements Visual impairment: reduced acuity relative afferent pupil defect diplopia Proptosis Severe headache or other features of intracranial involvement
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Neonates: consider gonorrhoea and *Chlamydia*** and send PCR swabs.
claims.source_text: Consider gonorrhoea and Chlamydia infections in neonatal presentation (send PCR swabs)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bilateral or painless (non-tender) swelling in a well child is more likely allergic.**
claims.source_text: Bilateral findings and/or painless (or non-tender) swelling in a well looking child is more likely to be an allergic reaction
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Admit, keep fasted until the need for surgery is clear, and seek ENT and ophthalmology advice urgently.** Consider urgent contrast CT of orbits and sinuses ± brain.
claims.source_text: Admission Keep fasted until need for surgery clarified Seek ENT and Ophthalmology advice urgently Consider urgent contrast enhanced CT scan of orbits, sinuses +/- brain … Urgent imaging and surgical consultation (ENT and ophthalmology) should be considered for any child with suspected orbital cellulitis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **FBE and blood culture.** ⚠️ **Lumbar puncture is contraindicated** — risk of raised intracranial pressure from possible intracranial extension.
claims.source_text: FBE and blood culture … Lumbar puncture is contraindicated due to risk of raised intracranial pressure secondary to possible intracranial extension
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat underlying sinus disease** (e.g. nasal decongestants, steroids), often guided by ENT.
claims.source_text: Treat underlying sinus disease eg nasal decongestants, steroids (often guided by ENT)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Orbital cellulitis IV: cefotaxime 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) 6-hourly or ceftriaxone 100 mg/kg (max 4 g) daily**; add vancomycin if MRSA is suspected.
claims.source_text: Cefotaxime 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) IV 6 hourly OR Ceftriaxone 100 mg/kg (max 4 g) IV daily If suspected MRSA, add vancomycin (see link for dosing)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **IV usually for at least 3–4 days, then oral amoxicillin/clavulanate 22.5 mg/kg (amoxicillin component, max 875 mg) twice daily — 10–14 days total.**
claims.source_text: Duration based on clinical severity and improvement. Usually at least 3-4 days, then switch to oral Amoxicillin with clavulanic acid (doses based on amoxicillin component) 22.5 mg/kg (max 875 mg) oral bd 10–14 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Inadequate Hib vaccination: treat as severe periorbital cellulitis.**
claims.source_text: If inadequate Haemophilus influenzae type B (Hib) vaccination, treat as severe periorbital cellulitis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severe:** investigate and manage as an inpatient, as for orbital cellulitis.
claims.source_text: Severe Inpatient investigations and management as per orbital cellulitis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Moderate:** inpatient or hospital-in-the-home; blood culture if febrile and unwell. Change to oral once improving; **if not improving or worse within 24–48 hours, manage as severe.**
claims.source_text: Moderate Inpatient management or consider Hospital In The Home (HITH) admission if available locally Consider blood culture if febrile and unwell … Once improving change to oral antibiotics If not improving or deteriorating within 24–48 hours, consider managing as severe periorbital cellulitis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Moderate or severe, IV:** cefazolin 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) 8-hourly **or** ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) daily (HITH) **or**, if MRSA suspected, clindamycin 15 mg/kg (max 600 mg) IV 8-hourly or oral. IV usually 1–2 days, then oral.
claims.source_text: Cefazolin 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) IV 8 hourly OR Ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) IV daily (HITH) OR If suspected MRSA, Clindamycin 15 mg/kg (max 600 mg) IV 8 hourly OR oral … Duration based on clinical severity and improvement. Usually 1-2 days, then switch to oral
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Moderate or severe, oral step-down:** as for mild periorbital cellulitis; if MRSA suspected, clindamycin 15 mg/kg (max 600 mg) three times daily. **Total 7–10 days.**
claims.source_text: When improving, switch to oral antibiotics as per mild periorbital cellulitis If suspected MRSA: Clindamycin 15 mg/kg (max 600 mg) oral TDS … 7–10 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mild periorbital cellulitis in a well child can often be treated orally if follow-up is assured: cefalexin 20 mg/kg (max 750 mg) three times daily for 7–10 days.**
claims.source_text: Periorbital cellulitis in a well child can often be treated with oral antibiotics if follow-up is assured … Mild periorbital cellulitis Not applicable Cefalexin 20 mg/kg (max 750 mg) oral TDS … 7-10 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Follow local susceptibility guidance**, including on community-acquired MRSA.
claims.source_text: Antimicrobial recommendations may vary according to local antimicrobial susceptibility patterns; please refer to local guidelines; these may include advice regarding community acquired MRSA
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss with the paediatric team** for suspected orbital cellulitis, moderate–severe periorbital cellulitis, or no improvement or deterioration after 24–48 hours.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Orbital cellulitis suspected Moderate-severe periorbital cellulitis present No improvement or deterioration after 24–48 hrs of therapy
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider transfer** for severe periorbital or orbital cellulitis, or suspected intracranial involvement (altered conscious state, seizures, focal neurological signs).
claims.source_text: Consider transfer when Severe periorbital cellulitis or orbital cellulitis present Suspecting intracranial involvement with altered conscious state, seizures or focal neurological signs
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge — mild:** oral course prescribed and follow-up assured. **Moderate:** after 24–48 hours of IV antibiotics with improvement, tolerating oral, follow-up assured.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Mild periorbital cellulitis: oral antibiotic course prescribed follow-up assured Moderate periorbital cellulitis: after 24–48 hrs of IV antibiotics and with improvement able to tolerate oral antibiotics follow-up assured
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Periorbital and orbital cellulitis' (Last updated December, 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Periorbital_and_orbital_cellulitis/, retrieved 2026-09-23
